items.reason: PDF p16 states that symptoms, signs and pathology test results support diagnosis, but the candidate only contrasts arbitrary exclusions. Removed as weak; the complete statement remains in the detailed source and is not represented as assessed.

PDF p20 is a repeated list of biochemical injury mechanisms. Its distinct relationships are assessed in organelle-targets (pp22–23), calcium-enzyme-effects (p24), ATP consequences (p28) and ros-target-effects (pp31–32); no duplicate list-recognition item retained.

The unpaired-outer-electron definition is preserved on PDF p29, but its candidate had implausible electron/proton distractors and was removed. The adjacent combined free-radical/ROS list and reactive-nitrite wording remain source restrictions; this page group is explicitly unassessed rather than counted as covered.

PDF p36 CCl4-to-fatty-liver route repeats the ribosome-detachment/protein-synthesis/lipid-deposition distinction assessed by ch1-part-02-ribosomes-fat on p28. The direct CCl3-species candidate was removed for implausible alternatives. Full p36 pathway remains in the source; no duplicate scored item retained.

PDF p5 lists receptor regulation/binding and protein-synthesis changes as adaptive mechanisms. Candidate removed because its four distractors were universal denials; list remains fully preserved, with no separate scored mechanism item claimed.

PDF p14 autophagy sequence is repeated in Chapter1 Part04 PDF pp4–7 and is assessed there by ch1-part-04-autophagy-substrate. No duplicate cross-part item retained; this original page remains cited in the study source.

PDF p20 ambiguous causal wording about structural synthesis increasing workload is restricted; clear cell enlargement and workload triggers are assessed in adaptation-types and hypertrophy-demand (pp18–21).

PDF p22 gene reactivation, contractile-protein switching and possible degenerative failure are preserved. Candidate removed for unrelated/absolute alternatives; these additional phenotype/outcome claims are not counted as assessed.

PDF p5 diagram repeats lysosomal fusion, uptake and residual processing. Primary-secondary, autophagy-substrate and uptake-processes assess its distinct relationships on pp3,7–8; no duplicate diagram-reading score retained.
PDF p6 repeats autophagic versus heterophagic processing and secondary lysosome formation; covered by primary-secondary and autophagy-substrate on pp3–8.

PDF p10 SER induction/solubility/excretion and unqualified alcohol–phenobarbital example remain in the detailed source. Both weak candidate sets were removed (universal or impossible alternatives); this page is not counted as assessed.

PDF p7 comparison diagram repeats reversible swelling versus destructive necrotic changes. Its distinct relationships are assessed by reversible-light, reversible-nuclear, no-return, mitochondrial-density and cytoplasmic-features on pp10–28.

PDF p16 introduces the calcium-mediated irreversible injury route, repeated in Part02 p24. Retained ch1-part-02-calcium-enzyme-effects assesses the same enzyme consequences; no duplicate cross-part score.
PDF p17 calcium/enzyme map duplicates Part02 p24 and ch1-part-02-calcium-enzyme-effects. Removed the repeated matching item while preserving both original page extractions.

PDF p25 digestion-versus-denaturation mechanism is assessed as a real contrast in ch1-part-06-coagulative-digestion (Part06 pp3,11). Leakage marker examples remain preserved but are not separately assessed by a weak item.

PDF p13 fungal renal abscess illustrates complete digestion/obliteration of architecture. This distinction is assessed in coagulative-preservation and coagulative-digestion on pp3,6,11; its duplicate example-only candidate was removed, while the full caption/image remains in the source.

PDF p18 repeats the fragmentation-to-apoptotic-body-to-removal morphology already assessed by ch1-part-07-apoptosis-morphology on pp17/21. The dedicated ligand-recognition candidate had implausible distractors and was removed; ligand detail remains unassessed in the source.

PDF p2 general accumulation locations and local/elsewhere origin/harmless/injurious scope remain faithfully in the source. Both candidate questions relied on only/must/always restrictions and were removed; this concept group is explicitly unassessed.

PDF p33 aortic-valve dystrophic calcification causing aortic stenosis remains a cited source fact. No retained question has four plausible same-domain alternatives from the named material; no unrelated options or outside valve-disease facts added.

PDF p35 lists metastatic deposition sites and says generally no dysfunction unless severe, exemplified by nephrocalcinosis. The candidate relied on absolute guarantees and unrelated definitions and was removed; distribution is not scored as exclusive and functional qualification remains unassessed.
